topics.name: Theme 1 Changing Places - Changing Economies
points: 1.1 Global urbanisation and global cities
1.1 Contrasting city case studies (LIC/NIC and HIC): causes of growth and ways of life
1.1 Urban challenges (poverty, housing, transport, waste) and strategies to manage urbanisation
1.2 Urban change in the UK: urbanisation, suburbanisation, counterurbanisation, re-urbanisation and infill
1.2 Rural change in the UK: commuter villages and depopulation
1.2 Distinctive urban zones; urban renewal and the brownfield/greenfield debate
1.2 Migration, commuting, teleworking and sustainable living
1.2 Changes in retail and leisure: out-of-town parks, online shopping, rural honeypots and major events
1.3 Measuring development and its limitations; LICs and NICs
1.3 Drivers of globalisation: trade, technology, geo-political links, culture, migration and MNCs
1.3 Causes and consequences of uneven development: MNCs, NIC growth, trade and fair trade
1.3 Long-term development aid and short-term emergency aid

topics.name: Theme 2 Changing Environments
points: 2.1 Coastal processes: weathering, mass movement, erosion, transport and deposition
2.1 Coastal landforms and human modification of coasts
2.1 Coastal management: hard and soft engineering, hold the line and retreat the line, Shoreline Management Plans
2.1 Climate change impacts on coastal communities and management challenges
2.2 The water cycle in river basins and flood hydrographs
2.2 River processes and landforms
2.2 Causes and consequences of river flooding, including flash floods
2.2 Hard and soft flood management and controversy over river management
2.3 Variability of the UK climate
2.3 Global atmospheric circulation and climate zones, including the hot semi-arid climate
2.3 Pressure systems, weather charts and associated hazards
2.3 Global distribution and changes in drought and tropical cyclones
2.3 Extreme events outside the UK: one high pressure and one low pressure event (causes, impacts, responses)
2.4 Climate change during the Quaternary period
2.4 The greenhouse effect and evidence for global warming
2.4 Consequences of climate change for farming, wildlife, water, population and tourism
2.4 Attitudes to climate change, global initiatives, and individual and UK government action

topics.name: Theme 3 Environmental Challenges
points: 3.1 Global biomes and their link to climate
3.1 Hot semi-arid grasslands and one other biome: interdependence, nutrient and energy flows, food webs, biodiversity
3.1 A small-scale UK ecosystem: benefits, management challenges and stakeholder views
3.2 Human use and modification of ecosystems
3.2 Damage to hot semi-arid grasslands and one other ecosystem at local and global scales
3.2 Conservation and sustainable management strategies
3.3 Global trends in water supply and demand; water footprints and water security
3.3 Over-abstraction and water transfer schemes in contrasting countries
3.3 Local management of supply and demand imbalances and international water issues
3.4 Physical processes making hot semi-arid regions vulnerable to desertification; changing distribution
3.4 Human causes of desertification and stakeholder viewpoints
3.4 Strategies to tackle desertification: NGOs and international responses

topics.name: Problem solving and decision making (all themes)
points: Part A: understanding an issue and its geographical context from resources
Part B: evaluating possible solutions to the issue
Part C: choosing a solution and justifying it in an extended response

topics.name: Part A Fieldwork methodologies, representation and analysis
points: Posing enquiry questions and hypotheses
Collecting evidence: sampling, quantitative and qualitative methods and secondary sources
Methodological approaches: transects, change over time, qualitative surveys and geographical flows
Processing and presenting fieldwork data
Analysing patterns and relating them to wider geographical knowledge
Drawing evidenced conclusions
Evaluating the enquiry: accuracy, reliability and bias

topics.name: Part B Conceptual frameworks in fieldwork
points: Place
Sphere of influence
Cycles and flows
Mitigating risk
Sustainability
Inequality

topics.name: Part C Applying geography to a UK context and decision making
points: Applying broad geographical concepts to a wider UK context
Making and justifying a decision
